data.name: Hades' Star
data.detailed_description:
In Hades' Star, you create and grow a space Empire over time, in a persistent galaxy that constantly evolves.

These are the star types discovered so far:

Yellow Stars


As the most stable star type, the Yellow Star offers a perfect setting to establish your permanent presence and plan your Empire's long term economy. All new players start in their own Yellow Star system and over time expand to discover and colonize more planets, set mining patterns, establish trade routes and neutralize the mysterious alien ships found throughout the Hades galaxy.

As the owner of a Yellow Star system, you have complete control over what other players have access to it. By establishing diplomatic relations, you can allow any other player to send ships to your system, and dictate your own terms for mining, trade or military cooperation.

Red Stars


Very early in the game, every player will build a Red Star Scanner, a station that allows them to jump ships to detected Red Stars. These stars have a small lifetime and will go supernova after 15 minutes.

The goal in the Red Star is to co-operate with any other players that have ships in that star system, defeat the NPC ships, retrieve Artifacts from the Red Star planets, and jump back before the Supernova. Artifacts can be researched in the home star and will yield necessary resources for trade, mining and combat advancements. Higher level Red Stars offer more challenging enemies and better rewards.

White Stars


Players can organize in Corporations. Besides helping each other, Corporations can also scan for White Stars. A White Star sees up to 40 players from two Corporations battle in the same star system for Relics, a resource that can be retrieved to upgrade the Corporation and give each member additional benefits.

Time passes by very slowly in White Stars: every match lasts for 5 days, giving Corporation members time to talk and coordinate their strategy. The Time Machine can be used to plan future moves, communicate them to other Corporation members, and see potential outcomes of future combat.

Blue Stars


These short lived stars only last for 5 minutes, during which the entire system is collapsing on itself. Each player can only send a single Battleship to the Blue Star. The 5 participating players combat each other, using their ship's modules and other NPC ships to destroy the other player ships and be the last one alive.

Blue Stars offer the fastest PvP action in the game. Regular participants receive daily and monthly rewards to advance their Empire.

reviews.review:
This might be a good example where deciding on a game by recent reviews would be a mistake. Just note how most of the negative reviews are from veteran players. That's because they were in love with the status and power they had in PvP and to some extent in PvE, no matter that it mostly consisted from unimaginative meta play to straight abusive exploitation of game imbalances. Methods available to a considerably greater degree to higher level players. See where this is going?
So when the dev decides to address these issues, the most impacted players claim he is hating them? /facepalm The only thing he actually seems to dislike is unsportsmanlike behaviour.
As to the game itself. It has been re-balanced, progress towards the start is faster than before, and slower than before towards the end. New tech added, new max level. Ship action feels slicker, new and more engaging tactics but also faster paced than it used to be. At its core, the game still remains a long term power growth sprinkled with rewarding tactical play, with a focus on 10 min pve co-op matches, with optional 3 min pvp or 5 day pvp matches. Balanced for cca 30 to 60 min of active play daily (maybe a bit more if we count the 5d pvp matches).
Btw: The monetisation is unobtrusive and optional. Which seems rare nowadays, and is in my experience sign of a thoughtful and mature development team.

Oh, and to address the biggest misconception I'm seeing in reviews, this game is NOT pay to win. This game might have the least efficient premium currency I've ever seen, and it for sure does not encourage you to buy it. I will say it is very worth it to buy the starter pack (I think it is around $5) if you think you will play the game for a while and you want to support the devs. There is a reasonably priced option of $5 for a small amount of "crystals" given over the course of the week, but all of the other bundles are intentionally very expensive and don't really do that much. I'm talking the $50 pack only gets me enough credits to match what I would get in regular shipments in 3 days, not exactly "Pay to win". You also get the premium currency fairly regularly in game, enough that when you get a new tech that you are really excited about you can usually have the "crystals" to speed it up right away.

Well, I went on far longer than I intended, but if you have any questions, feel free to find me on discord at Sensei Jason#0348. Hopefully this game gets far more popular, we need more enemy fleets to destroy!

수송품은 행성렙이 17~20렙 쯤 되었을때 배달할만한 보상금(유물대비)을 준다 그전엔 앵간히 수소가 썩어나지 않는한 건들지 말자
수송품 릴레이로만 적당히 소모하도록 하자
신경쓰인다? 싸구려 수송품만 뜬다? 그러면 행성에 유물을 하나 넣어두어라
특.히! 위성딸려있으면서 보상이 싼 행성들 어딘지 알지? 첫 시작섹터에는 앵간하면 넣어두자
한자리 클딧 보상주는 수송품 어따 쓰라는건지 -_=;
여하튼 행성 렙이 어느 정도 될때까지는 유물 캐서 갈아버리는게 훨씬 남는 장사다

본인의 유물캐는 마지노선은 2섹터이다
그 이상은 수소 수입대비 수소소모량이 급격히 늘어난다고 생각한다
3개 챙길 정도면 2.5칸까지는 달려볼만하다고 생각한다

화포와 레이저 고민하는 유저들이 많더라
'특정상황'에서만 레이저가 우위다 청성과 5적 빼곤 레이저는 거의 안쓴다고 보면 된다
화포 렙이 7렙이상이다? 레이저 버리고 화포로만 5적도는 사람이 많다
범용성면에서 레이저가 화포를 절대 이길수가 없다
왜냐 ? 듀얼레이저와 달리 레이저는 타겟이 바뀌면 과열된게 초기화 되기 때문이다
물론 클딧 노가다 면에선 4적노가다가 5적 도는 것보다우월하단 것을 염두해두었으면 한다
공개 4적 돌아보면 알것이다 생각보다 고렙함선들을 많이 볼수 있다는 것을

화물 톤수는 2톤 (2적유물 1개) 4톤(3~4적유물 1개) 8톤(3~4적2개) 12톤(4적3개 / 5적2개) 16톤(4적4개 / 6적 2개) 20톤(7적유물 2개)

괘찮은 게임
근데 굳이 컴퓨터로 이런 장르를 하고싶진 않기에.. 차라리 사이버펑크가 낫다.
